Bertrand paradox (probability)

Words: 80
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
Different precise measures on random chords give different probabilities; the phrase “random chord” does not select a unique probability distribution. In a circle of radius r, a chord exceeds the side of an inscribed equilateral triangle exactly when its midpoint distance from the center is below r/2. Uniform midpoint area gives probability 1/4, independent uniform endpoints give 1/3, and uniform midpoint distance gives 1/2. The difference is in the sampling laws, not a contradiction in probability theory.

Polygon probability for independent uniform rods (1−1/(n−1)!)

Words: 88
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
For n≥3 independent lengths with the uniform distribution on [0,1], the probability of forming a nondegenerate polygon is 1−1/(n−1)!. The necessary and sufficient condition is that every length is less than the sum of the others. The failure events are disjoint except on sets of probability zero. The sum of n−1 lengths has probability density function sn−2/(n−2)! on 0<s<1, by repeated convolution of probability densities. A specified rod is too long with probability ∫01​(1−s)sn−2/(n−2)!ds=1/n!; summing over the n rods proves the formula. For three and four rods the probabilities are 1/2 and 5/6.

Coverage of a sphere by random open hemispheres (1−2NN(N−1)+2​)

Words: 103
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
The probability that N≥1 independent uniformly oriented open hemispheres cover a sphere is the displayed quantity. Coverage fails exactly when their normals lie in a closed hemisphere. With probability one, no three normals are coplanar and no pair is antipodal; a closed hemisphere containing the normals can then be perturbed into an open one. Condition on the unoriented axes of the normals. Their N orientation signs remain independent fair bits, and the regions of a general-position great-circle arrangement realize exactly N(N−1)+2 of the 2N possible sign vectors. Each such vector corresponds to normals that fit into one open hemisphere, proving the complementary probability. The argument counts equiprobable orientation choices, not equal-area regions.

Pairwise independent events (P(Ai​∩Aj​)=P(Ai​)P(Aj​), i=j)

Words: 56
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
Pairwise independent events have factorizable two-event intersections. Independent events require the corresponding factorization for every finite subfamily, which is stronger. If three events have common probability s and every pair and triple intersect in the same event of probability q, pairwise independence requires q=s2, while full independence additionally requires q=s3. Both hold only for s=0 or s=1.

Point process

Words: 425 Articles: 8
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
A point process is a random locally finite configuration of points, usually represented as a random counting measure. A finite eigenvalue configuration of a random matrix is an example. Multiplicities and whether the process is simple should be specified.

Neyman-Scott process

Words: 44
Point process OurBigBook.com
A Neyman-Scott process places independent offspring clusters around points of a Poisson parent process, with an independently drawn offspring count and displacements. Poisson offspring counts make the offspring process conditionally Poisson given the parents, and therefore give a Cox process. Arbitrary offspring counts need not have that property.

Intensity measure of a point process (μ(A)=EΠ(A))

Words: 35
Point process OurBigBook.com
The intensity measure of a point process Π is the measure μ(A)=E[Π(A)]. It can have infinite total mass even when counts on bounded or finite-intensity sets are finite. For a Poisson random measure, this measure also specifies every finite-set count distribution.

Void probability functional (v(A)=P(M(A)=0))

Words: 97 Articles: 1
Point process OurBigBook.com
The void probability functional assigns to a measurable set the probability that it contains no atom of a random point measure. For a Poisson random measure of intensity μ, it is e−μ(A). The exponential void probabilities characterize a Poisson random measure result uses simplicity; doubling every atom of a Poisson measure preserves void probabilities but changes count distributions.

Exponential void probabilities forbid fixed atoms

Words: 52
Void probability functional OurBigBook.com
If bounded intervals have void probabilities e−λ(I) for Lebesgue measure λ, a fixed deterministic point x has zero chance of being an atom. Surround it by intervals of lengths tending to zero and use P(M({x})>0)≤1−e−λ(I). This holds for each fixed endpoint, not simultaneously for all real points of a nonempty point process.

Simple locally finite point measure (M=∑j​δxj​​)

Words: 115 Articles: 1
Point process OurBigBook.com
A point measure is a countable sum of Dirac measures. It is simple if all its atoms have mass one, and locally finite if every bounded set has finite mass. Simplicity lets fine enough cells count individual points, whereas occupation indicators would lose multiplicities in a nonsimple measure.

Dyadic occupancy approximation of a simple point measure (Mn​(J)=∑D∈Dn​, D⊂J​1{M(D)>0}​)

Words: 69
Simple locally finite point measure OurBigBook.com
For a fixed bounded interval with no atoms at its endpoints, the occupation count of fully contained half-open dyadic intervals increases to the true count of a simple locally finite point measure. Refinement cannot reduce occupancy. Finitely many distinct atoms in a bounding interval have positive minimum separation; for fine enough cells each atom lies alone, and every interior atom's cell is contained in the target interval. Thus the counts eventually agree, path by path.

Determinantal point process (Rk​(x)=det[K(xi​,xj​)]i,j=1k​)

Words: 36
Point process OurBigBook.com
A point process is determinantal with kernel K relative to a specified reference measure if every correlation function of a point process is the indicated determinant. A rank-m finite-rank projection kernel gives an exactly m-point process, whose symmetric joint density is det[K(xi​,xj​)]/m!.

Correlation function of a point process (Rk​)

Words: 62
Point process OurBigBook.com
The kth correlation function is the density of the kth factorial moment measure: integrating a nonnegative test function against Rk​ gives the expectation of its sum over ordered k-tuples of distinct points. For exactly m exchangeably labelled points with symmetric joint density fm​, it is m!/(m−k)! times the marginal density of k labels. It is not normalized to have total mass one.

Random matrix

Words: 435 Articles: 8
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
A random matrix is a matrix whose entries are random variables. Its eigenvalues form a random configuration, and its empirical spectral measure records their distribution with equal mass on each eigenvalue. Entry assumptions and normalization determine the spectral regime.

Wishart distribution (Wp​(ν,V))

Words: 132 Articles: 1
Random matrix OurBigBook.com
For integer ν, the sum ∑j=1ν​Xj​XjT​ of independent Np​(0,V) vectors has a Wishart distribution. Its positive-definite density extends to real ν>p−1 and is proportional to ∣W∣(ν−p−1)/2exp[−tr(V−1W)/2]. It is a conjugate prior for the precision matrix of a multivariate normal distribution. Its mean is νV.
The WinBUGS declaration dwish(R, nu) uses R=V−1; the density convention is documented in the NIMBLE BUGS-language manual. For ν=p=3 it is proper, while the expected inverse matrix does not exist: that expectation requires ν>p+1. Specifying a Wishart prior on precision is therefore a substantive covariance assumption.

Inverse-Wishart distribution (IWp​(ν,R))

Words: 42
Wishart distribution OurBigBook.com
If W∼Wp​(ν,R−1) has the Wishart distribution, then W−1 has the inverse-Wishart distribution. For ν>p+1, its expected value is R/(ν−p−1); below this threshold the matrix mean does not exist. It commonly models a covariance matrix, but couples the prior behavior of variances and correlations.

Empirical spectral measure (LN​=N−1∑i=1N​δλi​​)

Words: 37
Random matrix OurBigBook.com
For an N-by-N Hermitian matrix, the empirical spectral measure puts mass 1/N at each eigenvalue, counted with multiplicity. It is a probability measure. Integrating a test function against it gives the average of that function evaluated at the eigenvalues.

Wigner matrix (Xij​=N−1/2Yij​)

Words: 154 Articles: 2
Random matrix OurBigBook.com
A real Wigner matrix is a real symmetric matrix whose upper off-diagonal entries are independent centered copies of a fixed random variable, scaled to have variance of order 1/N. Diagonal conventions may vary and should be specified separately. A common version has variance-one unscaled off-diagonal entries and either zero diagonal entries or independent diagonal entries with a bounded second moment.

Centered truncation of a Wigner matrix (Xij​=N−1/2(Yij​1∣Yij​∣<C​−E[Yij​1∣Yij​∣<C​]))

Words: 98 Articles: 1
Wigner matrix OurBigBook.com
Truncate the unscaled entries of a Wigner matrix at a fixed threshold and subtract their expected values. The difference between original and truncated entries is N−1/2(ZC​−EZC​) with ZC​=Y1∣Y∣≥C​, so its variance is bounded by N−1E[Y21∣Y∣≥C​]. The centering term cannot be discarded for an asymmetric entry law.
Second moment bound for spectral truncation
Words: 50
Centered truncation of a Wigner matrix OurBigBook.com
For a fixed mean-zero variance-one real entry law, centered truncation of a Wigner matrix satisfies E[N−1Tr(X−X)2]≤t(C), where t(C)=E[Y21∣Y∣≥C​]→0. The spectral Lipschitz bound from Frobenius distance and Markov inequality give probability at most t(C)/ε2 for a spectral test-function discrepancy exceeding ε. Thus t(C)<ε3 works uniformly in matrix size. A varying entry-law family requires uniform second-moment tail decay instead.

Complex Wishart matrix (A=X∗X)

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Random matrix OurBigBook.com
A complex Wishart matrix is the Gram matrix of an n-by-m matrix of independent centered complex Gaussian random variables with an indicated variance convention. It is a positive semidefinite matrix. Percolation theory OurBigBook.com
In bond percolation on a directed graph, independently open each directed edge with probability p. The out-cluster of x consists of vertices reachable by open directed paths. In site percolation, independently open vertices and require every vertex of the directed path, including x, to be open. The same definitions allow a multigraph. The orientation matters: an infinite underlying connected graph need not contain an infinite out-cluster from a specified root.

Conditioning the root to be open changes the survival probability by a factor p and does not change the critical probability. This model gives an independent comparison process in the independent oriented-percolation comparison for the contact process.

On the oriented square lattice, edges run from (x,n) to (x±1,n+1) with x+n even. The critical probability is the infimum of parameters with positive survival probability. The incoming-edge coupling of site and bond percolation compares this threshold with that of oriented site percolation.

Alternating arms argument at the self-dual percolation parameter

At parameter 1/2, primal and dual bond percolation on the square lattice have the same probability distribution. Suppose an infinite percolation cluster exists. Large boxes meet it with probability tending to one. The square-root trick for positively associated events and quarter-turn symmetry imply that each side has an infinite exterior open arm with probability tending to one. The same holds for dual arms. A union bound then gives positive probability of primal top and bottom arms together with dual left and right arms.
Use a primal box [−r,r]2 and a dual box with sides at ±(r+1/2). Open only primal edges whose endpoints both lie in the primal box, preserving all outward and exterior arm edges. The two primal arms are joined inside. Planarity prevents the two alternating dual arms from joining: a proposed dual connection together with the inner boundary arc separates one primal infinite arm from infinity. Thus the modified configuration has two infinite dual clusters. Its positive probability by finite modification of Bernoulli percolation contradicts uniqueness of the infinite percolation cluster. Consequently the percolation probability at 1/2 is zero. This is often called Zhang's argument.

Vary the division point until the failure probabilities a,b of the two alternating primal arc types are comparable within a factor (1−p)−2. If the probability of no primal exterior arm is at most ε, then a3b3≤ε and both failures are at most (1−p)−1ε1/6. De Finetti theorem
Words: 146
Exchangeable random variables OurBigBook.com
For an infinite sequence of real exchangeable random variables, conditional on its invariant sigma-algebra of an exchangeable sequence, the coordinates are independent and identically distributed. In particular, for Borel sets A0​,…,Ap​,
E[∏k=0p​1Ak​​(Xk​)∣S]=∏k=0p​E[1Ak​​(Xk​)∣S].
(45)
Here is the core proof. Let Sm​ denote invariance under permutations of coordinates 0,…,m. Symmetrization as conditional expectation identifies the empirical average of each indicator with its conditional expectation on Sm​. The reverse martingale convergence theorem gives its limit conditional on S. Multiplying the averages sums over all ordered coordinate tuples, including repetitions. Symmetrization of the product itself sums over the distinct tuples. The fraction of repeated tuples is at most (2p+1​)/(m+1), so these bounded averages have the same limit. This proves the displayed factorization. Permutation invariance also makes the individual conditional laws identical. A regular conditional distribution on the real line packages that common law as a random probability measure, giving the equivalent mixture-of-iid formulation.

Invariance of A and the law shows that the conditional expectation on the second block is an equally good approximation. It is measurable with respect to the tail after index n. The L1 contraction of conditional expectation then bounds ∥F−E[F∣Gn​]∥1​ by twice the approximation error. The reverse martingale convergence theorem gives F=E[F∣⋂n​Gn​] almost surely. For mesh h, the risk-neutral up probability is (eρh−d)/(u−d). The log-price increment has mean (ρ−σ2/2)h+O(h2) and variance σ2h+O(h2). The Donsker invariance principle gives convergence of the log-price process to Brownian motion with this drift, hence of prices to the Black-Scholes model. Payoff-price convergence additionally uses continuity at almost every limiting path and uniform integrability for unbounded payoffs.

The unique equivalent martingale measure in the one-stock Cox--Ross--Rubinstein model assigns each up move probability
q=U−DR−D​=u−d1−d​
(97)
and each down move probability 1−q. Under this measure the discounted stock is a martingale.

For a payoff h(ST​,MT​) with Mt​=maxs≤t​Ss​, the pair (St​,Mt​) is a sufficient Markov state for valuation. If an independent restarted stock path has initial value y, terminal value z, and running maximum w, then the continued payoff is
g(x,m,y,z,w)=h(yxz​,max{m,yxw​}).

Thinning of a point process

Words: 35
Probability theory OurBigBook.com
Thinning removes points from a point process according to a retention rule. Independent retention with probability p(x) changes the intensity measure to p(x)μ(dx). For a Poisson point process, the retained and removed point processes are independent Poisson processes.
